claim: places: rehovot
quote: was launched into space from Palmahim Beach
correction: Launch site was Palmahim Beach (coast south of Rishon LeZion), not Rehovot; quote: 'was launched into space from Palmahim Beach'

claim: wording: Ashdod's port described as 'deep-water'
quote: The artificial port, enclosed by breakwaters, is southern Israel’s only outlet to the Mediterranean
correction: No opened source calls it 'deep-water'; say 'its port (an artificial harbour enclosed by breakwaters) opened in 1965' (Britannica quote above; JVL: 'The port was opened in 1965').

claim: Over 260,000 Jews from Arab and Muslim countries had arrived by 1951
quote: Immigration to Israel (1948-1951) by Major Countries of Origin (thousands): Yemen and Aden 48.3; Morocco, Tunisia, Algeria 45.4; Turkey 34.5; Libya 31.0; Iran 21.9; Egypt 8.8 (Sicron, in Naor ed., Olim and Ma'abarot 1948-1952)
correction: Understated. Sicron's 1948-51 figures for Yemen/Aden, North Africa, Turkey, Libya, Iran and Egypt alone total c. 190,000; Israel State Archives table gives Iraq 124,226 (to end 1952, most arriving 1951) and 'Total Muslim countries 377,251' for May 1948-end 1952 (https://www.jewishvirtuallibrary.org/immigrants-to-israel-1948-1952). Suggest 'over 300,000 by the end of 1951'.

claim: emigration from Morocco had been banned since 1959
quote: banned Jews from moving to Israel from 1959 until February 1961
correction: Sources disagree on the start of the ban. Encyclopaedia Judaica (JVL, https://www.jewishvirtuallibrary.org/morocco-virtual-jewish-history-tour): 'on May 13, 1956, an order was issued forbidding Jews to leave for Israel' and 'In 1959, all Zionist activity was forbidden in Morocco'. Suggest: 'emigration to Israel had been banned since 1956 (Zionist activity outlawed in 1959)' or cite both.

claim: Egoz sank with 44 aboard
quote: the Egoz , one of the Misgeret’s smuggling ships, foundered at sea, and 42 Jewish immigrants drowned
correction: Encyclopaedia Judaica gives 42 Jewish immigrants drowned; no opened source gives 44. Use '42 Jewish emigrants drowned' (or cite a source for 44 if the builder has one).

claim: estimates range from 80,000 to 100,000
quote: between November 1961 and spring 1964 more than 90,000 Jews left for Israel
correction: Opened sources give 'more than 90,000' (Encyclopaedia Judaica) and 'more than 97,000' (israeled.org); no opened source supports an 80,000 low bound. Suggest 'estimates range from over 90,000 to about 97,000' and effects.aliyah low bound 90000.

claim: completeness: summary omits wounded and the later reduction/pardons of the sentences
quote: Forty-three people were killed in the shooting, and 13 injured. ... None of the policemen served a full sentence, and many of them were pardoned by then president Yitzhak Ben-Zvi.
correction: Optionally add: 13 wounded; none of those convicted served a full sentence and many were pardoned by President Ben-Zvi (Times of Israel). Israeli casualties: none reported.

claim: part of a policy to increase the Jewish population of the Galilee
quote: One of Israel’s development towns, Karmiʼel is the first Jewish town in an area settled almost entirely by Arabs.
correction: No opened source states the policy aim in those words; Britannica supports: 'the first Jewish town in an area settled almost entirely by Arabs'. Reword to that, or add a source naming the Galilee-settlement policy.

claim: In 1950 most of the remaining Arab residents of Majdal were moved to the Egyptian-held Gaza Strip (displacement 2,000-2,700)
quote: It originally consisted of the houses of the city Majdal, whose last Arab inhabitants, 2,400 in number, were "transferred" to Gaza, Lod and Ramle - an unusual step even at that time.
correction: Haaretz gives 2,400 last Arab inhabitants, transferred to Gaza and also to Lod and Ramle (inside Israel). Suggest: 'the remaining c. 2,400 were moved, most to Gaza and some to Lod and Ramle'. The 2,000-2,700 range in effects covers 2,400.

claim: Death toll: sources differ (contemporary UN figures lower than 69)
quote: the attack on Qibya ... resulted in the death of fifty-three Arab inhabitants and the destruction of more than forty dwellings
correction: Note the disagreement: the MAC resolution of 15 Oct gave 42 dead and 15 wounded (count while bodies still under rubble); UNTSO Chief of Staff Bennike reported 53 dead on 27 Oct 1953; 69 is the later commonly cited total (JVL). Suggest 'killing 69 villagers (UN observers reported 53 at the time)'.

claim: Neutrality: casualty record lists only Palestinian dead; the Israeli victims of the Yehud attack named in the summary are omitted
quote: a house in the Israel village of Yahud, which caused the death of two small children and their mother
correction: Add Israeli casualties of the triggering Yehud attack: 3 killed (a mother and two children). For the raid itself, MAC also recorded 15 wounded villagers (S/PV.630); Israeli casualties in the raid: none reported in the sources opened.

claim: neutrality: summary/casualties omit Palestinian civilians killed in the Gaza Strip during the occupation (Khan Yunis, Rafah)
quote: the Director has received from sources he considers trustworthy lists of names of persons allegedly killed on 3 November, numbering 275 individuals, of whom 140 were refugees and 135 local residents of Khan Yunis. ... lists of names of persons allegedly killed at Rafah on 12 November, numbering 111, of whom 103 were refugees, seven local residents, and one an Egyptian.
page: UN doc A/3212/Add.1 (UNRWA Director's special report), 15 Dec 1956
correction: Add casualties.palestinians killed c. 386 (UNRWA name lists: 275 at Khan Yunis on 3 Nov and 111 at Rafah on 12 Nov 1956; a further 66 in smaller incidents 1-21 Nov). Israel disputed the circumstances (UNRWA: 'there is some conflict in the accounts given as to the causes of the casualties').

claim: neutrality: casualties omit British and French dead
quote: British and French casualties in the invasion of Suez, which coincided with Israel’s thrust into the Sinai desert, were 82 killed and 129 wounded.
correction: Add casualties.uk_france killed 82 (AP).

claim: choice 3: 'Seek arms and a security guarantee from France without going to war', associated with Sharett
quote: Sharett’s foreign policy had an American orientation in that he looked to America for political support, a security guarantee, economic aid, and arms. ... Since the alliance with France was predicated on Israel’s willingness to go to war against Egypt, the debate over orientation merged with the other great debate on the question of preventive war.
page: Avi Shlaim, 'Israel between East and West, 1948-56'
correction: Sharett's no-war line sought arms and a security guarantee from the United States, not France; the French connection (Peres, Dayan) was tied to going to war. Relabel: 'Seek US arms and a security guarantee without going to war' - advocate Moshe Sharett (Shlaim: 'Sharett was firmly opposed to war'), Foreign Minister until June 1956.

claim: Purpose: to reduce malaria
quote: The goal of eradication of malaria was actually achieved in 1949, irrespective of the draining project.
correction: Malaria had already been eradicated by 1949 'irrespective of the draining project' (JVL); KKL-JNF lists farmland, settlement, stopping evaporation losses and peat, not malaria. Remove 'and reduce malaria' or say 'malaria control was a long-standing argument for drainage, though malaria had been largely eliminated by 1949'.

claim: Kiryat Gat began in 1954 as a ma'abara (event dated 1954)
quote: Kiryat Gat was founded in 1955 near the tell then held to be the site of Philistine Gath.
correction: No opened source supports a 1954 ma'abara start; EJ dates the founding to 1955. Suggest dating the event 1955 or citing a source for the 1954 camp.

claim: Near the depopulated village of Iraq al-Manshiyya
quote: West of the present municipal area lay the village Fāluja, which was abandoned in 1948. It was destroyed after the "Ten Plagues" Operation in the War of Independence
correction: Iraq al-Manshiyya could not be verified from an opened source (palestineremembered/palquest blocked). EJ names al-Faluja, abandoned in 1948 and destroyed after Operation Yoav, west of the town. Suggest 'near the depopulated village of al-Faluja' or add a Khalidi citation for Iraq al-Manshiyya.

claim: Initially settled by families from Morocco
quote: Of the adult population (1968), about 50% were immigrants from Mediterranean countries, mainly North Africa, 20% from Eastern Europe, mainly Romania
correction: No opened source names Moroccan families as the first settlers; EJ gives 1968 origins: c. 50% North Africa, 20% Eastern Europe (mainly Romania). Suggest 'settled mainly by immigrants from North Africa'.

claim: wording: UNEF 'guaranteeing' passage through the Straits of Tiran to Eilat until 1967 (places: straits_of_tiran, eilat)
quote: This detachment maintained an observation post and kept the Strait of Tiran under constant watch. ... However, just before he arrived in Cairo, President Nasser announced the closure of the Strait of Tiran.
correction: UNEF observed rather than guaranteed passage: 'a UNEF detachment at Sharm el-Sheikh kept the Straits of Tiran under watch, and they stayed open to Israeli shipping until Egypt closed them in May 1967'. The UN record also notes UNEF's stationing 'would require Egyptian consent'.

claim: effects note: UNRWA registered 957k in 1950
quote: When the Agency began operations in 1950, it was responding to the needs of about 750,000 Palestine refugees.
correction: UNRWA's own figure for 1950 is 'about 750,000 Palestine refugees'. No opened source gives 957k registered in 1950; drop it or give it only with a primary citation.

claim: Mitzpe Ramon founded in 1951 (same-year event)
quote: מצפה רמון | MIZPE RAMON | ... | שנת ייסוד: 1954
page: CBS list of localities 2024, row Mizpe Ramon, column 'שנת ייסוד'
correction: CBS gives the founding year of Mitzpe Ramon as 1954, not 1951. Haaretz (c. 2011, https://web.archive.org/web/20120207125819/http://www.haaretz.com/print-edition/features/israel-s-grand-canyon-town-struggles-to-shake-off-sand-1.411479): 'The town, which was founded 55 years ago' (i.e. c. 1956). Move Mitzpe Ramon out of this 1951 event (CBS 1954) or say 'a road-workers' camp from 1951 (unsourced) became Mitzpe Ramon, founded 1954 per CBS'.

claim: Israeli paratroopers attacked an Egyptian army base near Gaza City
quote: attacked an Egyptian military camp, the Gaza Stationmaster's house and a concrete water-pump house supplying part of the Gaza area ... Another group of the Israeli Army ... ambushed a military truck carrying a Lieutenant and thirty-four other ranks
correction: Base attack verified; 'paratroopers' not verified in any opened source (UN: 'a force of the Israeli Army'). Also note the second action: an ambush of an Egyptian reinforcement truck south of Gaza.

claim: 37-38 Egyptian soldiers killed
quote: The casualties on the Egyptian side were found to be 36 military personnel and two civilians killed, 29 military personnel and two civilians wounded.
correction: UN MAC finding: 36 Egyptian military personnel and 2 civilians killed (Egyptian complaint: 1 officer, 35 soldiers, a civilian and a seven-year-old boy); 29 soldiers and 2 civilians wounded. Change to '36 Egyptian soldiers and 2 Palestinian civilians, including a seven-year-old boy'.

claim: Neutrality: civilian casualties in Gaza omitted from the casualty record
quote: As a result of this attack 1 officer, 35 soldiers, a civilian and a seven year old boy were killed. 29 soldiers, a civilian and a 9 year old boy were wounded
correction: Add casualties.palestinians (Gaza civilians): killed 2, wounded 2; set egypt killed to 36 (military).

claim: UN condemnation (context, not in summary): Security Council Resolution 106 condemned the attack
quote: Condemns this attack as a violation of the cease-fire provisions of Security Council resolution 54 (1948) and as inconsistent with the obligations of the parties under the General Armistice Agreement between Egypt and Israel
page: S/RES/106, Resolution of 29 March 1955, adopted unanimously
correction: Summary omits the unanimous UNSC condemnation (Res. 106, 29 March 1955); consider adding for balance, as done for Qibya and Samu.

claim: sources disagree on the 20% allocation
quote: While Begin agreed, he was adamant that the Irgun retain 20% of the ammunition. Ben-Gurion rejected the offer, however, maintaining that there could only be one army
correction: Sources disagree. Lapidot (JVL) says Ben-Gurion accepted 20% for the Jerusalem Battalion; the World Jewish Congress account says he rejected the Irgun retaining 20%. Per the contract, the summary should note both and cite both.

claim: casualties effect: palestinians killed [400,400]
quote: It is estimated that inside the city, the total number of dead exceeded 400. ... it is likely that the number of those killed in the city itself and those who died during the march of death totaled close to one thousand.
correction: Same source: more than 400 killed inside the city and close to 1,000 including deaths on the march. Make the range [400, 1000] or mention the march deaths.

claim: neutrality: Israeli military casualties at Lydda not listed
quote: A number of Israeli soldiers were killed, and as a result, the Israelis were even more brutal in their reprisals on the city's residents.
correction: Add Israeli soldiers killed during the capture of Lydda. The opened source gives no number ('A number of Israeli soldiers were killed'); give a sourced figure or say 'unspecified number'.

claim: in about 380 flights
quote: required the charter of close to 450 flights flown by Alaska Airlines
correction: Sources give 430-450 flights, not 380: JDC Archives 'close to 450 flights'; Alaska Airlines: 'The airlift would continue through 1950 with Alaska Airlines making more than 430 flights, using two DC-4s and a C-46 aircraft.' (news.alaskaair.com/alaska-airlines/on-eagles-wings/)

claim: dates: June 1949 to September 1950 (date_end 1950-09-24)
quote: JDC planned, organized, and financed the mass exodus, which began in December 1948 and ended on September 19, 1950
correction: JDC Archives: airlift began December 1948 and ended 19 September 1950. Change date_end to 1950-09-19 and say 'December 1948 (mainly from mid-1949) to September 1950'; no opened source supports 24 September or a June 1949 start.

claim: Israeli-Syrian clashes over the works followed in 1964-67
quote: But Syria started work on the projects of diversion, resulting in armed clashes with Israel during late 1964 to 1966 (see Section X). Owing to Israel's forceful reaction, the work on the diversion was suspended in 1966
page: Israel MFA Selected Documents 1947-1974, ch. VII
correction: Clashes specifically over the Syrian diversion works ran late 1964 to 1966 (work suspended 1966); suggest 'Israeli-Syrian clashes over the Arab diversion works followed in 1964-66'. Wider border tension continued into 1967.

claim: neutrality: displaced Palestinian population not quantified
quote: He states some 25,000 additional refugees have been forced out of Galilee
correction: Add the displaced Palestinian Arab figure: about 25,000 refugees forced out of Galilee (UN Mediator's representative Servoise, reported by the US Minister in Syria, 3 Nov 1948). No opened source gives casualty figures for Israeli, ALA or civilian dead; say 'not quantified in opened sources' or add a sourced figure.

claim: demolishing dozens of houses
quote: 125 houses, the village medical clinic, a 6-classroom school and a workshop had been completely demolished. In addition, one mosque and 28 houses had been damaged.
correction: UN observers counted 125 houses plus the clinic, a school and a workshop demolished in as-Samu and 28 houses and a mosque damaged; a further 15 stone huts were destroyed at Kh. Jimba (para. 15). Replace 'dozens of houses' with 'about 125 houses, a clinic and a school'.

claim: Jordanian casualties reported as 16 killed and 54 wounded
quote: The United Nations Military Observers were provided with the death certificates of 14 Jordanian Arab army personnel (including the death certificate for an aircraft pilot) and of 3 civilians killed during the incident. The United Nations Military Observers were also given medical certificates of 37 military personnel and seven civilians who had been wounded and hospitalised
correction: UN Secretary-General's report S/7593 (18 Nov 1966): death certificates for 14 Jordanian army personnel and 3 civilians (17 dead); 37 military and 7 civilians wounded and hospitalised. A captured Jordanian major also died in Israeli custody (para. 31). A US estimate (FRUS 1964-68 v.18 doc 338) gave 'about 50 deaths—half of them Jordanian soldiers'. Suggest casualties.jordan killed [14,25] and add the civilian population line below.

claim: neutrality: Palestinian civilian casualties of as-Samu omitted
quote: the death certificates of 14 Jordanian Arab army personnel (including the death certificate for an aircraft pilot) and of 3 civilians killed during the incident ... medical certificates of 37 military personnel and seven civilians who had been wounded
correction: Add affected population: Palestinian civilians (residents of as-Samu/Hebron area, then Jordanian citizens): 3 killed, 7 wounded and hospitalised (UN S/7593); 125 houses demolished. e.g. casualties.palestinians {killed:[3,3]}.

claim: a national unity government was formed on 1 June 1967 with Moshe Dayan as defence minister
quote: Minister of Defense Levi Eshkol 12/01/1966 - 05/06/1967 Alignment Moshe Dayan 05/06/1967 - 17/03/1969 Rafi
correction: The Knesset's official record dates Dayan's term as Minister of Defense, and the entry of Gahal ministers Menachem Begin and Yosef Sapir, from 5 June 1967 ('Moshe Dayan 05/06/1967 - 17/03/1969 Rafi'; 'Menachem Begin 05/06/1967 - 17/03/1969 Herut-Liberal Bloc'). No source I opened gives 1 June; suggest 'agreed on 1 June, formally from 5 June' only if a source for 1 June is added, otherwise say 'at the start of June'.

claim: by December 1967 about 245,000 people crossed from the West Bank and Gaza Strip to Jordan and about 11,000 from Gaza to Egypt (Bowker)
quote: (a) About 200,000 persons (of whom about 93,000 were refugees registered with UNRWA) who had moved from the West Bank to the East Bank in Jordan; ... (c) About 35,000 persons (of whom 3,000 were UNRWA-registered refugees in the Gaza strip) who had moved across the Suez Canal from the Gaza strip or Sinai.
correction: Bowker's 245,000/11,000 figures could not be opened (print only). Primary UN figure (Secretary-General's report A/6797, 2 Oct 1967, para. 159): about 200,000 moved from the West Bank to the East Bank (about 93,000 of them UNRWA-registered refugees) and about 35,000 moved across the Suez Canal from the Gaza Strip or Sinai. Suggest using these UN figures.

claim: other historians estimate 280,000-325,000 Palestinians displaced overall
quote: After Jordan launched its attack on June 5, approximately 325,000 Palestinians living in the West Bank fled to other parts of Jordan, primarily to avoid being caught in the cross-fire of a war.
correction: Upper figure 325,000 (West Bank) confirmed by JVL (which also frames the flight as voluntary; the UN report documents expulsions/demolitions too); the lower bound 280,000 was not found in any opened source. The UN Secretary-General's report gives about 350,000 fled from all occupied areas, of which about 200,000 from the West Bank and about 35,000 from Gaza/Sinai (A/6797 para. 159: 'roughly estimated at about 350,000'). Suggest: 'estimates range from about 235,000 (UN, West Bank and Gaza/Sinai, Sept 1967) to 325,000 (West Bank alone)'.

claim: from the Golan Heights, estimates of Syrians who fled or were expelled range from about 80,000 (Morris) to about 116,000 including Palestinians (McDowall)
quote: (b) About 110,000 persons according to Syrian sources and not more than 85,000 according to Israel sources (of whom about 17,000 were UNRWA-registered refugees) who had moved from the south-western corner of Syria, mainly to the areas of Damascus and Dera'a
correction: Morris and McDowall (print) could not be opened. Primary UN figure: about 110,000 according to Syrian sources and not more than 85,000 according to Israeli sources, including about 17,000 UNRWA-registered Palestinian refugees (A/6797 para. 159). The same report (para. 14) says the original population was 'some 115,000 according to Syrian sources, and some 90,000 according to Israel sources' and that 'this entire population had left the area, except for' a few villages.

claim: neutrality: omits Egyptian civilians displaced from Sinai (e.g. East Kantara)
quote: The President of the municipality declared that out of a population of about 15,000, only 1,116 persons had remained.
correction: Add Egyptian civilians from Sinai: the UN report counts about 35,000 persons who moved across the Suez Canal from the Gaza Strip or Sinai (para. 159(c)), and in East Kantara 'out of a population of about 15,000, only 1,116 persons had remained' (para. 151).

claim: Egyptian fatality estimates roughly 9,800-15,000
quote: The death toll on the Arab side was 15,000 Egyptians, 2,500 Syrians, and 800 J[ordanians]
correction: Upper bound 15,000 confirmed (JVL). Lower bound 9,800 (Gawrych, print) not opened; opened sources give 'over 10,000 killed and missing for Egypt' (Brunel BURA record 2438/12122) and 'Egypt's casualties numbered more than 11,000' (Britannica, https://web.archive.org/web/20250102060126/https://www.britannica.com/event/Six-Day-War). Suggest 'roughly 10,000-15,000'.

claim: Jordanian fatalities about 700-800
correction: 800 Jordanian dead is supported (JVL overview: '15,000 Egyptians, 2,500 Syrians, and 800 J[ordanians]'), but other opened sources give much higher Jordanian losses: JVL casualty table 6,094; Britannica 'with 6,000 for Jordan' (archived https://web.archive.org/web/20250102060126/https://www.britannica.com/event/Six-Day-War); Brunel record '6,000 for Jordan' (killed and missing). Sources disagree; suggest 'about 700-800 according to some sources, up to about 6,000 killed and missing according to others'.

claim: neutrality: omits Iraqi military losses
correction: Iraq also fought (JVL overview: 'On June 4, Iraq joined the military alliance with Egypt, Jordan, and Syria'); JVL casualty table lists Iraqi losses as 2,000 (an estimate; 'Figures for the Arab armies are estimates'). Add Iraqi losses or note them as uncertain.

claim: the extension took in East Jerusalem and about 70 km2 of surrounding West Bank land
quote: the endorsement by the Knesset of the annexation of 71,000 dunams [1dunam = ¼ acre] to the Israeli Jerusalem. Only 6,000 of these dunams were within Palestinian Jerusalem. The rest of the territory was confiscated from some 28 villages in the Jerusalem periphery.
correction: About 70 km2 (71,000 dunams) in total, of which about 6 km2 was Jordanian East Jerusalem and the rest (about 65 km2) land of some 28 surrounding villages. Suggest: 'took in about 70 km2, including East Jerusalem (about 6 km2) and land of 28 surrounding West Bank villages'. (Source is a Palestinian scholar, Sufyan Abu-Zayda, Palestine-Israel Journal.)

claim: Allon is described as 'Deputy Prime Minister' when he proposed the plan in July 1967
quote: Deputy Prime Minister Yigal Allon 01/07/1968 - 17/03/1969 ... Minister of Labor Yigal Allon 12/01/1966 - 01/07/1968
correction: In July 1967 Allon was Minister of Labour; he became Deputy Prime Minister only on 1 July 1968 (Knesset: 'Deputy Prime Minister Yigal Allon 01/07/1968 - 17/03/1969'; Haaretz also calls him 'labor minister Yigal Allon' in 1967). Suggest 'Labour Minister (later Deputy Prime Minister) Yigal Allon'.

claim: in 1968 most ministers treated it as the basis of settlement policy
quote: An important discussion about this issue took place at a meeting of the Alignment's diplomatic committee on April 20, 1968. ... most of them - with the exception of Dayan and Shimon Peres ... - expressed backing for the "Allon plan" as the basis of the policy.
correction: The source says most speakers at the Alignment party's diplomatic committee (20 April 1968), not 'most ministers', backed the Allon plan 'as the basis of the policy' (of negotiations with Jordan), with Dayan and Peres dissenting. Suggest: 'in 1968 most Alignment leaders, though not Dayan, backed it as the basis of policy'.

claim: wording completeness: summary omits the fourth principle in the same sentence
quote: no peace with Israel, no recognition of Israel, no negotiations with it, and insistence on the rights of the Palestinian people in their own country.
correction: The resolution's sentence continues 'and insistence on the rights of the Palestinian people in their own country'; for accuracy the summary could quote it in full.

claim: Jordanian dead about 40-84
quote: Jordan repel an Israeli attack on Karameh where 86 Jordanians lost their lives
correction: The official Jordanian figure is 86 killed (Jordan Times citing Petra: '86 Jordanians lost their lives'); the 40-84 range could not be verified in any opened source. Suggest 'about 40-86 (86 per the Jordanian government)'.

claim: Palestinian fighters killed about 100-200
quote: By most accounts, the Palestinians, who knew the Israelis were coming, took heavy casualties, and up to half of their several hundred lightly armed fighters were killed.
correction: No opened source gives 100-200 explicitly; Village Voice (2004) says 'up to half of their several hundred lightly armed fighters were killed', and the Oxford LearnPalestine module says fighters 'fought to the end, and many were killed or captured'. Suggest 'up to half of several hundred Palestinian fighters' or keep 100-200 only with a source.

claim: neutrality: omits Palestinian civilian/property losses in Karameh camp
quote: most of Karameh camp was destroyed, and 175 homes razed to the ground.
correction: Add that most of Karameh refugee camp was destroyed and 175 homes razed (Oxford LearnPalestine).

claim: on land requisitioned 'for military purposes', according to minutes of a July 1970 meeting in Defence Minister Dayan's office
quote: In minutes of meeting in then-Defense Minister Moshe Dayan's office, top Israeli officials discussed how to violate international law in building settlement of Kiryat Arba ... the expropriation of Palestinian land for ostensibly military purposes when the true intent was to build civilian settlements
correction: Confirmed: 1970 minutes from Dayan's office, land expropriated for 'ostensibly military purposes' (Haaretz headline: 'Secret 1970 Document Confirms First West Bank Settlements Built on a Lie'). The month 'July' could not be confirmed (article body paywalled); say 'a 1970 meeting'.

claim: about 750 athletes from 28-29 nations took part
quote: In total 774 Para athletes (578 men and 196 women) from 28 countries competed in 181 medal events across 10 sports.
correction: IPC: 774 athletes from 28 countries. Suggest 'about 770 athletes from 28 countries'.

claim: about 163,000 Soviet Jews settled in Israel in the late 1960s and 1970s
correction: 163,000 not found in an opened source. The NJRC table gives Soviet Jewish emigrants going to Israel in 1970-1978 summing to about 132,000 (999 + 12,819 + 31,652 + 33,477 + 16,816 + 8,531 + 7,279 + 8,348 + 12,231 = 132,152), with 1979 still to come. Suggest 'about 130,000 in 1970-1978 (roughly 150,000 including 1979)' or cite a source for 163,000.

claim: from the mid-1970s a growing share chose the United States instead (47% in 1976)
correction: In 1976, 49.0% of Soviet Jewish emigrants went elsewhere than Israel (NJRC table: 1976 'Elsewhere 7,004 ... 49.0%'); the paper's text says 'By 1976 only one half of the Soviet Jewish emigrants were making aliyah.' Use 49% (about half).

claim: Israeli military deaths about 694-1,424 depending on period counted
quote: The Israeli death toll between June 15, 1967, and August 8, 1970, was 1[,424 soldiers and more than 100 civilians]
correction: 1,424 confirmed (JVL; also JVL Six-Day War page: '1,424 Israeli soldiers and more than one hundred civilians were killed'), but it covers 15 June 1967 - 8 Aug 1970. The lower figure 694 was not found in any opened source. Also add Israeli civilian deaths: 'more than one hundred civilians'.

claim: Egyptian deaths estimated at 2,882-10,000
quote: 1,424 Israeli soldiers and more than one hundred civilians were killed; Egypt suffered approximately five thousand dead.
correction: Neither 2,882 nor 10,000 was found in an opened source; JVL gives 'approximately five thousand' Egyptian dead. Suggest 'about 5,000 (estimates vary)' unless a source for the range is added.

claim: neutrality: omits Egyptian civilian displacement from the canal cities
quote: the main cities on the west bank of the Canal were destroyed, and about a million inhabitants had to be evacuated deep into Egypt.
correction: Add: canal-zone cities were largely destroyed and about a million Egyptian civilians were evacuated (JVL).

claim: neutrality: omits other Arab states' losses (Iraq, Jordan, Saudi Arabia, Morocco)
correction: Add the estimated losses of other Arab expeditionary forces: Iraq 125, Jordan 23, Saudi Arabia 100, Morocco 200 (JVL table; estimates). JVL overview also notes an Iraqi division of about 18,000 men fought on the Golan.

claim: estimates of Palestinian dead range from about 2,000 to 3,400 (Arafat claimed far more)
quote: Arafat says 25,000 Palestinians are killed; other sources estimate 2,000 to 4,000 Palestinian militants and an unknown number of civilians killed.
correction: Opened sources give 2,000-4,000 Palestinian militants plus an unknown number of civilians (CIE), and AFP: 'Estimates ... range widely, between 2,000 and 30,000. Palestinians have revised down the toll to 3,000' (https://www.dailynewsegypt.com/2010/09/16/jordan-plo-turn-page-on-black-september-but-fears-remain/). Arafat claimed 25,000. The 3,400 upper bound was not found; suggest 'about 2,000-4,000 fighters plus civilians (Arafat claimed 25,000)'.

claim: neutrality: Palestinian civilians and displacement to Syria and Lebanon
quote: they turned on the PLO, killing and wounding thousands of Palestinians and forcing thousands more to seek refuge in Syria and Lebanon.
correction: Add that thousands of Palestinians fled to Syria and Lebanon and that civilian deaths are uncounted ('an unknown number of civilians killed', CIE).

claim: after meeting them in April, Meir called them 'not nice'
quote: One month later, 6,000 Black Panthers and their supporters hold a massive demonstration in Jerusalem. After the protesters clash with police, Meir is quoted as saying the Panthers "are not nice people."
correction: Opened sources place the remark after the violent May 1971 demonstration, not after the April meeting (CIE; Unpacked: 'It was this violent protest that led Golda Meir to remark that the Panterim were "not nice guys."'). Suggest 'after the May clashes Meir called them "not nice"'.

claim: a public committee acknowledged ethnic and socio-economic gaps and welfare spending rose
quote: three days after the first demonstration, the cabinet agreed to release extra funds for social programs. A daily newspaper proclaimed, "The 'Panterim' Helped the Cabinet 'Find' the Budget."
correction: Extra social funding is confirmed (after the first demonstration, March 1971). The public committee's findings were not found in an opened source; drop or source that part.

claim: shot down by Israeli F-4 fighters after failing to respond to interception signals
quote: Israeli Air Force jets were then sent up to intercept the plane. He said they signaled the airliner to land, using internationally accepted signals but the pilot disregarded them and disregarded warning shots
correction: Interception and ignored signals confirmed (as the Israeli army's account, per JTA 22 Feb 1973). The aircraft type 'F-4' was not stated in any opened source; say 'Israeli fighter jets' or add a source for F-4 Phantoms.
